explanations.explanation: Yes, Ephraim does not notice. Foreigners consume his strength, but he does not notice (Hosea 7:9). It's like a cookie box slowly emptying while nobody ever looks inside. The sad part is that it's his own strength going.

Not quite. The verse says the foreigners consume his strength, “…but he does not notice.” The verse doesn't mention any fighting. The picture is of his strength draining away while Ephraim doesn't see it, friend.
Begging would at least mean Ephraim saw the problem. But the verse says foreigners consume his strength, “…but he does not notice.” That's the whole sad picture, friend.

Half of that is right. His hair is streaked with gray, but the verse ends “…but he does not know.” That second half is the whole point. I check my mustache in the mirror every morning, so I'd catch it fast.

That's the right call. The gray is really there, but the text says “Even his hair is streaked with gray, but he does not know.” So Ephraim is aging and has no clue. Gray hair is one thing, but missing it entirely is something else.

Not quite. The verse says Israel's arrogance testifies against them, “…yet they do not return to the LORD their God…” They are not returning (Hosea 7:10). The evidence is on the table and they still walk the other way.
Right, they do not return. Hosea 7:10 says “despite all this, they do not seek Him.” After all of that, they still don't go to Him. Even a loud witness doesn't turn their feet around.

That's it. The verse says the dove is “…calling out to Egypt, then turning to Assyria.” Those are two big nations, and Ephraim runs between them. A dove that can't pick a rooftop will wear out its wings.

Moab and Edom aren't the ones in this verse. Hosea 7:11 says Ephraim is “…calling out to Egypt, then turning to Assyria.” I think it's an easy mix-up with all those names floating around. Egypt and Assyria are the pair.
Those two are famous names, but they're not in this verse. The dove calls out to Egypt, then turns to Assyria (Hosea 7:11). Egypt first, then Assyria. Nice try, though.

Yes, His net. The LORD says, “As they go, I will spread My net over them; I will bring them down like birds of the air.” It fits the bird picture from the verse before. Birds in a net don't get to pick a direction anymore.

Wings make sense with all the bird talk, but that's not what the verse says. The LORD says, “As they go, I will spread My net over them…” This is a net, not a cover. He says He will bring them down like birds of the air.
A tent is a good guess, but it isn't here. The LORD says, “…I will spread My net over them…” The picture is birds being brought down. Nobody is getting a cozy place to sleep.
Yes, redeem. The LORD says, “Though I would redeem them, they speak lies against Me.” He would redeem them. That one word shows what He was ready to do, and it makes the lies hit harder.

Yes, lies. The verse says, “Though I would redeem them, they speak lies against Me.” They speak lies against the very One who would redeem them. That's a heavy line, friend, and it's worth slowing down on.
Abandon isn't the word here. Hosea 7:13 says, “Though I would redeem them…” The LORD is the One who would redeem. The people are the ones who strayed and rebelled.
Praise would be lovely, but it's not in the verse. Hosea 7:13 says, “Though I would redeem them, they speak lies against Me.” Praise has left the building.
No blessings in this verse. It says they “…speak lies against Me.” even though He would redeem them. The word that fits the first blank is redeem. Blessings never show up.

Not this time. The LORD says, “They do not cry out to Me from their hearts when they wail upon their beds.” The wailing is there, but the verse says they do not cry out to Him from their hearts. So the statement flips what the verse says.

Right. Hosea 7:14 says they do not cry out to the LORD from their hearts when they wail upon their beds. The LORD says it plainly: “They do not cry out to Me from their hearts…” That makes the statement False, friend.

That's the one. The verse says, “They slash themselves for grain and new wine, but turn away from Me.” This is a heavy part, friend. They go to painful lengths for grain and new wine, and the verse says they turn away from the LORD.
Silver and gold aren't what the verse names. It says, “They slash themselves for grain and new wine…” Those are harvest goods. The verse ends with them turning away from the LORD.

Horses and chariots aren't in this verse. Hosea 7:14 says, “They slash themselves for grain and new wine, but turn away from Me.” Grain and new wine are what they're after. It's an easy mix-up, since people mention those all the time.

Yes, it's true. The LORD says, “Although I trained and strengthened their arms, they plot evil against Me.” The verse gives both facts. He trained and strengthened their arms, and they plot evil against Him.

The verse says otherwise. Hosea 7:15 reads, “Although I trained and strengthened their arms, they plot evil against Me.” So it's true on both counts. He trained them and strengthened them, and they plot evil against Him.
That's the one. Hosea 7:16 says, “They turn, but not to the Most High; they are like a faulty bow.” A faulty bow can't be trusted to hit what you aim at. They turn, but not toward the Most High.

A cracked jar is a fair picture, but it's not the one here. The verse says, “They turn, but not to the Most High; they are like a faulty bow.” The picture is a bow that can't be counted on. A jar just sits there.
A dry well would be a sad image, but the verse picks a different one. It says, “they are like a faulty bow.” That's a tool that won't do its job when it's needed. Keep your bucket, friend.

Yes, cursing. The verse says, “Their leaders will fall by the sword for the cursing of their tongue…” That's the reason the verse gives for the leaders falling by the sword. Cursing is the word that fills the blank.
Praying would be a very different story. The verse says their leaders will fall by the sword “…for the cursing of their tongue…” The word in the verse is cursing, not praying.

Singing would be nicer, but that's not it. Hosea 7:16 says, “Their leaders will fall by the sword for the cursing of their tongue…” Cursing is the word. Their tongues are being used for the wrong job.
